name: Buahan, A Banyan Tree Escape
positioning: Open-air rainforest retreat of private pool bales in the highlands north of Ubud, built around a 'No Walls, No Doors' design philosophy
best_for: Couples who want open-air pool bales with rainforest, valley and mountain views
Travelers drawn to Balinese culture, nature walks and spa rituals

facts.text: Buahan is in the highlands north of Ubud in Payangan, Gianyar, surrounded by tropical forests with views of Bali's seven peaks.
The resort follows a 'No Walls, No Doors' design philosophy of open-air living spaces and uninterrupted views.
Each private bale is an interpretation of a traditional Balinese pavilion, positioned to frame a distinct view of the surrounding landscape.
Every bale has a private pool, open-air living spaces and uninterrupted views of the surrounding landscape.
The bales are built from locally sourced and reclaimed materials, including Ulin wood.
The bales have no walls, just curtains for privacy and roll-down bamboo shades for rain.
Bathrooms have hand-hammered copper bathtubs and carved wooden mirrors made by Balinese carpenters.
Toja Spa is an open-air spa named after the Indonesian word for water.
Toja Spa is spread over open-air bamboo pavilions overlooking the Ayung River.
The outdoor swimming pool has panoramic views of the jungle and nearby mountains.
Open Kitchen, the signature restaurant, celebrates locally sourced ingredients, seasonal harvests and Indonesian culinary traditions.
Every stay includes daily breakfast and a daily five-course dinner at Open Kitchen for two guests.

highlights.text: The Seven Peaks Pool Bale has panoramic views of Bali's seven peaks emerging with the morning light.
The Above the Waterfall Pool Bale sits above a cascading waterfall, surrounded by rainforest.
The Soul Freedom Journey is a guided purification ritual at the resort's own waterfall, beginning with making a Canang Sari offering.
On the Sandikala Walk, guests walk through the rice fields at twilight with a local farmer, learn about the Subak irrigation system and watch the fireflies.

considerations.text: In the open-air bales, guests can expect changing weather, natural sounds and occasional encounters with local wildlife and insects.
The dry season from April to October is ideal for outdoor activities and clear mountain views; November to March is the green season.
Each bale is designed for a maximum of two adults.
